adversarial-nli.description: Natural language inference (entailment/contradiction/neutral) on examples adversarially collected to fool existing models.

aider-polyglot.description: 225 Exercism coding exercises across 6 languages, scored inside Aider's real edit loop (including a second attempt after seeing failing tests) as a proxy for agentic coding-assistant quality.

aime.description: Real yearly American Invitational Mathematics Examination problems, repurposed as a fresh, contamination-resistant-ish annual AI benchmark.

algotune.description: Whether a model can optimize existing code to run measurably faster than a reference implementation while staying correct.

androidworld.description: Autonomous control of real Android apps across 116 dynamically-parameterized tasks spanning 20 apps.

arc.description: Grade-school multiple-choice science questions (Easy + Challenge splits) — NOT the same benchmark as ARC-AGI below, despite the shared name.

arc-agi-1.description: Novel visual-abstraction grid puzzles — infer a transformation rule from a few demonstration pairs and apply it to a held-out test grid, with almost no reliance on world knowledge.

arc-agi-2.description: A harder ARC-AGI successor, curated specifically to defeat brute-force search solvers that had started clearing v1 without genuinely generalizing.

arc-agi-3.description: Small interactive video-game-like environments an agent must explore, form a hypothesis about, and act in over multiple steps — a shift from static puzzles to interactive/embodied reasoning.
arc-agi-3.unit_label: % of public demo set solved (official ARC-AGI-3 leaderboard, bare model + minimal harness)

big-bench-hard.description: 23 hand-picked "hard" tasks from BIG-Bench where earlier models scored below average human raters — multi-step logical/algorithmic/commonsense reasoning.

blueprint-bench-2.description: Whether an agent can construct an accurate 2D floor plan of an apartment from a set of interior photographs, scored against the true room layout.

bool-q.description: Naturally-occurring yes/no reading-comprehension questions paired with a supporting Wikipedia passage.

points.org: Large Model Systems Organization,University of California (UC) Berkeley

browsecomp.description: Persistent, multi-hop web browsing to surface hard-to-find, entangled facts — designed to resist saturation by non-agentic models.

chartqa.description: Question answering over bar/line/pie charts, requiring both visual reading and arithmetic reasoning over the chart's data.

chess-puzzles.description: Best-next-move identification from chess positions (in FEN notation), judged against the Stockfish engine — a lightweight spatial-reasoning/planning probe.

codeforces-elo.description: Model solutions submitted to real Codeforces-style competitive-programming judging, reported as a human-comparable Elo rating.

common-sense-qa-2.description: True/false commonsense-knowledge statements, built adversarially via a human-vs-model "gotcha" collection game.

cursorbench.description: Ambiguous, multi-file coding tasks pulled from real Cursor IDE sessions — comprehension, bug-finding, refactoring, review.

docvqa.description: Question answering over scanned/photographed document images (forms, reports, invoices), requiring layout- and text-aware reading, not just OCR.

frontiermath.description: Original, unpublished research-to-exploratory-level math problems written by professional mathematicians, all-or-nothing scored, no partial credit.

gaia.description: Real-world questions requiring reasoning, multimodal handling, web browsing, and tool use — easy for humans, hard for AI assistants.

gdpval.description: Real work-product tasks (documents, slides, CAD, audio/video) across 44 occupations, graded by blind pairwise comparison against a human expert's actual deliverable.

gpqa-diamond.description: 198 graduate-level, "Google-proof" science questions in biology, chemistry, and physics — skilled non-experts with internet access score only ~34%.

points.org: Allen Institute for AI,University of Washington
Tsinghua University,University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC),Shanghai AI Lab,Peking University,Shanghai Jiao Tong University,CUHK Shenzhen Research Institute

hellaswag.description: Commonsense "what happens next" sentence completion, built via adversarial filtering against weaker models.

hle.description: 2,500 expert-vetted, frontier-difficulty questions across math, science, and humanities, explicitly designed to resist saturation for years.

humaneval.description: 164 hand-written Python programming problems, graded by functional correctness (pass@1) against hidden unit tests.

imo.description: The real International Mathematical Olympiad — AI systems opportunistically entered against the same problems as human competitors since 2024.

ioi.description: The real International Olympiad in Informatics — a competitive-programming olympiad AI systems have been tested against since 2024.

lambada.description: Predicting a passage's final word where broad discourse context (not just the last sentence) is required to get it right.

livecodebench.description: Competitive-programming-style coding problems continuously collected after each model's training cutoff, to reduce contamination.

livecodebench-elo.description: A separate, Elo-scored competitive-programming variant of LiveCodeBench ("LiveCodeBench Pro") — not on the same scale as the pass@1 version.

math.description: 12,500 competition-style math problems (AMC/AIME-sourced) across 7 subject areas and 5 difficulty levels.

points.org: Allen Institute for AI,University of Washington

mathvista.description: Mathematical reasoning that requires reading visual context — charts, geometry diagrams, figures — not just text.

mbpp.description: 974 crowd-sourced, entry-level Python problems (description + reference solution + tests), graded pass@1.

metr-cross-domain-time-horizon.description: Re-derives the time-horizon doubling trend across ~9 other domains (math, science QA, coding, computer use, self-driving) to test whether it generalizes beyond software.
metr-cross-domain-time-horizon.unit_label: approx doubling time (months) of domain-specific time horizon ('~2 years')

points.unit: doubling time (months) of domain-specific time horizon

metr-time-horizon.description: The length of task (in human-expert-equivalent hours) a model can complete autonomously with 50% success — METR's flagship autonomy-duration metric.

mirrorcode.description: Reimplementing a real command-line program from scratch by observing only its input/output behavior, not its source code.

mle-bench.description: Real end-to-end ML engineering on 75 curated Kaggle competitions, scored by "any-medal rate" against the competition's actual leaderboard.

mmbench.description: Fine-grained multimodal ability across 20 categories, using a circular-evaluation protocol (answer choices rotated) to reduce lucky guessing.

mmlu.description: Multiple-choice knowledge across 57 subjects (humanities, STEM, social science, professional exams) — the field's original general-knowledge headline number.

mmlu-pro.description: A harder, 10-choice, more reasoning-heavy successor to MMLU built specifically to un-saturate it.

mmmu.description: College-exam-level multimodal reasoning across 30 academic subjects, using real exam figures/diagrams that require expert subject knowledge to interpret.
mmmu.unit_label: % accuracy (MMMU-Pro, overall -- harder 10-option variant; used because this snapshot did not report a standard MMMU-validation score)

mystery-game-puzzles.description: Best-next-move identification in an undisclosed game's mid-game positions — the game's identity is kept secret specifically to block benchmark-specific preparation.

omni-math.description: 4,428 olympiad-level competition math problems across 33+ sub-domains with human-annotated difficulty ratings.

openai-ai-self-improvement-evals.description: Can a model replicate real internal OpenAI engineering pull requests, or diagnose real unsolved internal research bottlenecks — a direct proxy for "can it do an AI researcher's job."

points.unit: % pass@1 (OpenAI-Proof Q&A - diagnosing real internal research/eng bottlenecks)

osworld.description: Real, executable computer-use tasks (GUI + CLI) in genuine desktop OS environments, execution-graded against a 72%-scoring human baseline.

Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new) computer use - extended steps

points.unit: % binary accuracy (OSWorld 2.0 - harder long-horizon successor benchmark)

otis-mock-aime-2024-2025.description: Practice AIME-style contest problems (Olympiad Training and Inspiration Sessions) used as an additional fresh math-benchmark source.

points.org: Allen Institute for AI,University of Washington

paperbench.description: Whether an agent can replicate a real ICML Spotlight/Oral paper from scratch — understand it, write the code, run the experiments — against an author-reviewed rubric.

points.unit: % Code-Dev score (partial-credit variant that scores only code, not execution)

piqa.description: Physical commonsense reasoning — choosing which of two ways to accomplish a everyday physical goal makes more sense.

re-bench.description: Head-to-head AI-agent-vs.-human-expert performance on 7 open-ended ML research-engineering tasks under matched time budgets.

points.model: Best AI agents (Claude 3.5 Sonnet / o1-preview, best-of-k)
points.unit: ratio: agent score / human-expert score, at 2-hour equal time budget
ratio: human score / top-agent score, at 32-hour equal time budget

rli.description: The Remote Labor Index — whether AI agents can complete real, economically valuable freelance work (dev, design, architecture, data, video) to a professional-acceptance standard.

scicode.description: Code synthesis for real scientific-research problems across 16 natural-science subfields, with scientist-written gold solutions.

science-qa.description: Multimodal, multiple-choice science questions (often with images/diagrams) that also require a supporting explanation.

simpleqa.description: Short-answer factual recall (no retrieval/tools) on deliberately obscure-but-answerable trivia, graded correct/incorrect/not-attempted.

simpleqa-verified.description: A de-duplicated, rebalanced, relabeled 1,000-question refinement of SimpleQA (Google DeepMind).

superglue.description: A harder successor to GLUE bundling several difficult natural-language-understanding tasks into one suite.

swe-bench-lite.description: A smaller, cheaper-to-run 300-problem subset of the original SWE-bench.

swe-bench-multimodal.description: SWE-bench extended to issues that involve screenshots, UI mockups, or diagrams.

swe-bench-pro.description: A harder, 1,865-problem SWE-bench successor across 41 actively-maintained repos, designed to resist the contamination that hit the original.

swe-bench-verified.description: Whether an agent can resolve real GitHub issues — generate a patch that passes the repo's actual hidden tests — on a 500-problem, human-filtered subset.

tau-bench.description: Tool-using dialogue agents in customer-service domains (retail, airline), graded on task completion AND compliance with the company's stated policy.

points.model: Claude-3.7 Sonnet High (HAL Generalist Agent scaffold)

terminal-bench.description: Agent competence in real shell/terminal environments on long-horizon, multi-step tasks including recovery from failed tool calls.

truthfulqa.description: Whether a model avoids repeating common human misconceptions across 817 adversarially-written questions in 38 categories.

vending-bench.description: Long-horizon coherence of an autonomous agent running a simulated vending-machine business over very long task sequences.

vending-bench-dollars.description: Vending-Bench scored by mean simulated-dollar net worth the agent ends with.

webarena.description: End-to-end task success across 812 long-horizon tasks on self-hosted, fully-functional websites (e-commerce, forums, GitLab, a CMS).

winogrande.description: Large-scale, adversarially-filtered pronoun-resolution commonsense reasoning (a scaled-up Winograd Schema Challenge).
